item.text:
**2024 events**

1. Srettha pushed Thailand’s signature cash-transfer stimulus forward in April 2024. Cabinet approved the 500 billion baht “digital wallet” plan, which would give 10,000 baht to 50 million Thais; Reuters also noted it was framed as a growth stimulus but drew debt and fiscal-risk criticism.
Source: [Thailand's $13.5 billion household stimulus plan gets cabinet approval](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thailands-cabinet-approves-135-billion-digital-wallet-handout-3390007), Reuters via Investing.com, April 23, 2024.
Question IDs: 8B (best-fit economic policy / implementation).

2. His premiership ended abruptly on August 14, 2024. Thailand’s Public Relations Department said the Constitutional Court removed him for violating ethical standards after appointing Pichit Chuenban, whose prior bribery-related contempt case became the center of the ruling.
Source: [Prime Minister Srettha Thavisin Has Been Removed from Office](https://thailand.prd.go.th/en/content/category/detail/id/48/iid/315614), Public Relations Department, August 14, 2024.
Question IDs: governance / ethics / legal vulnerability, plus 8B insofar as it reflects administrative judgment.

3. The same digital-wallet agenda also showed implementation problems by August 2024. Reuters reported early registration snags, delayed launch timing, and criticism from economists and former central bankers who called the scheme fiscally risky.
Source: [Thailand's flagship $14 billion handout scheme suffers early snags as millions rush to register](https://www.yahoo.com/news/thailands-flagship-14-billion-handout-072635149.html), Reuters via Yahoo News, August 1, 2024.
Question IDs: 8B (policy execution, fiscal management).

**Background context, not a discrete event**

4. External forecasters saw a modest recovery under his government, not a boom. The World Bank’s July 2024 monitor projected 2.4 percent growth in 2024, driven by private consumption, tourism, and goods exports, while flagging fiscal sustainability pressures and the need for more targeted support.
Source: [Thailand Economic Monitor July 2024: Unlocking the Growth Potential of Secondary Cities](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/thailand/publication/temjuly2024), World Bank, July 2024.
Question IDs: 8B (macro management / growth performance).

5. Thailand’s central bank described 2024 as a slow, structurally constrained recovery. In its June 12, 2024 MPC statement, the Bank of Thailand said growth would be driven by domestic demand, tourism, and government disbursement, with exports subdued and structural headwinds still weighing on the economy.
Source: [Monetary Policy Committee’s Decision 3/2024](https://www.bot.or.th/en/news-and-media/news/news-20240612.html), Bank of Thailand, June 12, 2024.
Question IDs: 8B (economic conditions / policy environment).
